title: Routing Audit Entry
description: One immutable entry in the routing audit log. Entries are appended, never amended: a decision and what it later turned out to cost are two events, because the second is not known when the first is made. `selected` records which Deployment a connection target was set to and on what grounds; `attributed` records who the ledger says actually paid for the requests that followed; `released` records that a profile stopped pointing at one, so a log cannot show a route still standing after it was rolled back.

id.description: Content hash of the entry, computed like an Evidence id over the entry with `id` removed.

event.description: `selected` a connection target was set, `attributed` the ledger reported who paid for what followed, `released` the profile stopped pointing at one. A restore that undoes a switch is a selection; a restore that undoes the first connect is a release, and calling it a selection of nothing would be a record of something that did not happen.

grounds.description: Why this Deployment and not another. `explicit` means the operator named it, `recommendation` means a ranking chose it, `existing` means the profile already pointed at it, `interactive` means it was picked from a list, `restore` means a rollback put it back. Recording the outcome without this cannot answer why, which is what an auditable route has to answer.

recommendationId.description: The Recommendation this selection came from, when grounds is `recommendation`. Its own record carries the rule, the profile version and the evidence behind the ranking, so the audit cites it rather than copying it.

selectionId.description: The `selected` entry this attribution belongs to.

attribution.description: What the billing ledger reported for the requests that followed the selection. Absent requests are not an absence of cost: settlement lags, and `unconfirmed` says so rather than claiming either outcome.

method.description: How the attribution was established. `gateway` and `request-id` name individual requests; `ledger-window` is a difference between hourly billing buckets and can be polluted by another machine on the same account. Recording which one produced a figure keeps an approximation from being read as an exact one.

requestIds.description: The requests this attribution covers, where they are individually known.
